| Family | Attacks | IAMWatch ACTIVE, right origin | Single-event rules (R1-R5) | GuardDuty, any finding in window | GuardDuty, finding names the origin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 30 | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | n/a | n/a |
| S2 | 30 | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | n/a | n/a |

| S5 | 30 | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | n/a | n/a |
| X1 | 30 | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | 0/30 (0%; 95% CI 0-11%) | n/a | n/a |
| X2 | 30 | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | 0/30 (0%; 95% CI 0-11%) | n/a | n/a |
| X3 | 30 | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | 0/30 (0%; 95% CI 0-11%) | n/a | n/a |
| X4 | 30 | 30/30 (100%; 95% CI 89-100%) | 0/30 (0%; 95% CI 0-11%) | n/a | n/a |
| **All** | 270 | **270/270 (100%; 95% CI 99-100%)** | 150/270 (56%; 95% CI 50-61%) | n/a | n/a |

Rule hits are computed offline from the same raw CloudTrail events that the stack received; GuardDuty findings are matched to an attack when their event window overlaps the attack ("any finding" is the generous reading) and, in the last column, when the finding names the attacking user. Rules never name the origin of a chain.

A full IAM download plus graph build took 146.3 s here (download 145.9 s, build 0.42 s), so a periodic scan adds that time plus on average half its interval to every detection.
